blocks.text: A developer does not memorize everything: they build a map connecting a goal, a file, a command, and evidence. Every experiment should answer one small question and produce a verifiable result. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Like a laboratory notebook: the recipe alone is insufficient; you record what was tested and observed.

Open Windows PowerShell from the Start menu. winget installs VS Code without assuming it already exists; if winget is unavailable, download the official installer from code.visualstudio.com and enable Add to PATH. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

Before any command, note the current directory, target file, and initial state. These three anchors prevent changing the wrong project or blaming a new change for an older problem. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

After the action, preserve the exact command, useful output, and your conclusion in a log. An error then becomes learning data rather than an opaque failure. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

blocks.text: The terminal always has a current directory; every relative path starts there, while an absolute path names the full location. A command acts on the target obtained after that resolution. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: The current directory is your position on a map; “..” goes up one street and an absolute path gives the full address.

Get-Location answers “where am I?” and Get-ChildItem answers “what is here?”. Run them together before a path-dependent command. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

Set-Location changes only terminal context, not files. -LiteralPath tells PowerShell to treat path characters literally, which matters for spaces and apostrophes. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Resolve-Path confirms a target before reading or modifying it. This check is essential whenever a command can write, move, or delete. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

blocks.text: VS Code is a structured view of the workspace: Explorer shows where code lives, Search shows where a concept is used, and Problems connects a diagnostic to an exact line. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: It is a workshop: Explorer is the shelf, the palette is the toolbox, and Problems is the quality-control board.

Use Ctrl+P to open a file by name and Ctrl+Shift+F to search text across the project. Intention-based navigation is more reliable than long manual browsing. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

Hovering a TypeScript symbol shows its type, F12 opens its definition, and Shift+F12 finds usages. Follow these links to understand the real flow before changing a shared function. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

After a change, inspect Problems and then Source Control to review changed lines. Save only an understood edit and verify related diagnostics disappear. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

blocks.text: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser, npm installs the package tree described by package.json and package-lock.json, and an npm script launches a local tool in a reproducible environment. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Node.js is the engine, package.json the parts list, package-lock the exact blueprint, and npm the mechanic assembling everything.

node --version confirms which runtime version answers in this terminal. An incompatible version can fail a project before your code is even read. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

npm ci follows package-lock.json exactly and suits a clean install; npm install may recalculate and update the lock when adding a dependency. The lock guarantees the same resolution on every machine. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

npm run dev favors fast feedback and stays active, whereas npm run build compiles and validates production output. A page visible in development therefore does not prove it can be deployed. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.
